newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: BHP says force majeure not issue at Ok Tedi.
newsitem.headline: BHP says force majeure not issue at Ok Tedi.

text.p: Australia's The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd (BHP) on Friday said force majeur was not yet an issue at its Ok Tedi copper operation in Papua New Guinea.
The Ok Tedi mine is unable to deliver concentrates to port because of unseasonally dry weather.
BHP barges copper from the mine to Port Moresby Harbour on the Fly River, but the river level is now too low for the barges. Storage of copper concentrates at the port have run dry.
"At the monent we have been able to supply our customers' requirements to date," BHP spokesman Vincent Bull said by telephone from the Papua New Guinea capital, Port Moresby.
"There are no shipments outstanding to our customers.
"Customers can call for shipments when they are required, but we have not got any outstanding at present, so it would be very premature to be talking about force majeure at the moment."
Ok Tedi ships on average around 50,000 tonnes of concentrate each month, but Bull said this could be equivalent to between just one and several shipments a month.
The last shipment loaded last week, he said.
"We are doing a rain dance and waiting," another BHP spokesman said.
Ok Tedi is 52.6 percent owned by Australia's Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd, with Canada's Inmet Mining Corp owning 17.4 percent and the rest held by the Papua New Guinea government.
Dry weather in other parts on PNG earlier this week forced the Porgera gold mine to suspend mill throughput as well.
